content: The use of intermittently scanned continuous glucose monitoring (isCGM) and real-time continuous glucose monitoring (rtCGM) systems is prevalent in diabetes management, with each offering distinct advantages tailored to the specific needs of patients. Clinical research has demonstrated that both isCGM and rtCGM are effective in lowering hemoglobin A1C levels and enhancing the duration of time patients maintain their blood glucose levels within the target range, known as Time in Range (TIR). However, rtCGM is generally associated with superior outcomes in the management of hypoglycemia. This is primarily due to its ability to provide real-time alerts and continuous feedback, which enable timely interventions to prevent or address episodes of low blood glucose.
